problem: Slow-fast / dual-system VLN methods pass sub-goals one-way from a high-level planner to a low-level executor. Execution-time progress and deviation signals are not fed back, so the two modules drift out of alignment and replanning is delayed. Prior error-correction methods (DAgger variants, CorrectNav) also need costly multi-round data flywheels.
motivation: Long-horizon VLN in continuous environments suffers from compounding control errors and route drift. Robust navigation therefore needs explicit tracking of semantic progress and timely, on-demand correction. The paper's observation is that the executor is best placed to detect completion or deviation, so it should trigger the planner rather than the planner running on a fixed schedule.
key_idea: Two independent Qwen2.5-VL-3B agents (intention and execution) communicate bidirectionally: the executor emits status tokens (continue, sub-goal done, off-track) that trigger the intention agent to generate regular or corrective language sub-goals. Action-CoT and a one-round reflective data pipeline support the executor's control and the intention agent's corrections.
insight: Ablations show that Action-CoT's latent coarse-route query improves R2R-CE SR from 52.8 to 60.0 (SPL 50.1 to 57.2). Decoupling the two agents beats a unified 7B VLM (SR 62.8 vs 57.3), even with fewer total parameters. Executor-triggered intention calls beat fixed-interval calls (SR 62.8 vs 61.8 for every 4 steps and 59.4 for every 12 steps), so execution feedback is a better update criterion than a fixed cadence. Competitive results come from about 1.6M samples, versus about 12M for DualVLN.
method: Intention agent: Qwen2.5-VL-3B that, given the instruction, recent RGB history and a request token (R regular or C corrective), generates a language sub-goal or a corrective sub-goal; it needs no goal detector.

Execution agent: separate Qwen2.5-VL-3B that grounds the sub-goal into N_q short-horizon waypoint controls (dx, dy, cos, sin, stop logit) and emits a status token: VLNBOA (continue), VLNBOR (sub-goal done), VLNBOC (deviation).

Action-CoT: path-conditioned dual-query scheme in which learnable navigation queries first predict a coarse long-horizon route; that route embedding then conditions the action queries. The route loss is weighted by beta=0.1.

Reflective data pipeline: one round of policy rollouts collects failures, a privileged expert with the environment graph gives recovery trajectories, Qwen3-VL-32B writes descriptions, and a checker filters hallucinations. This yields about 100k samples, with straight-move transitions subsampled and stop episodes augmented.

Two-stage training: Stage I is Action-CoT pretraining of the executor on NavForSee expert data (1.3M RxR-CE and 0.2M R2R-CE samples). Stage II trains the intention agent autoregressively and the executor on waypoints plus a status-token loss, with no gradient between agents.
Event-driven closed-loop inference: the intention agent produces the initial sub-goal, then the executor's status token decides whether to act or call the intention agent (R or C).

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B x2 (intention agent and execution agent, separate parameters, fine-tuned; execution agent adds MLP waypoint heads)
setting.training_data: NavForSee expert demonstrations on R2R-CE and RxR-CE (~1.3M RxR + 0.2M R2R samples) plus ~100k reflection-augmented recovery samples; ~1.6M total; no ScaleVLN or other large-scale pretraining data
setting.observation: monocular RGB current + history frames (no depth, panorama or odometry)
setting.action_space: predicted relative waypoints (dx, dy, heading, stop) in continuous environment
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged expert with environment graph is used only for training-data generation)

numbers.extra: ~1.6M samples, R2R+RxR+one-round reflection data; monocular RGB only
numbers.evidence: Table 1: comparison on VLN-CE benchmarks, R2R Val-Unseen; ReflectVLN (Ours) row

numbers.extra: ~1.6M samples, R2R+RxR+one-round reflection data; monocular RGB only

numbers_note: Ablation tables (Action-CoT, unified vs decoupled, trigger interval) report additional R2R-CE val-unseen numbers not listed as main-method rows.
results: ReflectVLN reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 62.8 / SPL 58.5 / NE 4.19 and RxR-CE val-unseen SR 66.0 / SPL 57.2 / NE 3.98 with monocular RGB only. On RxR it beats DualVLN (SR 61.4, SPL 51.8) and CorrectNav* (SR 63.1). On R2R it ties DualVLN's SPL (58.5) but trails its SR (64.3). It uses a smaller budget (2x3B, ~1.6M samples) and invokes the intention agent once per 9.63 steps.
limitations: Efficiency is measured only as intention-call frequency, not latency or FLOPs; the decoupled vs unified comparison is not parameter-matched (2x3B vs 7B).
Recovery data comes from a single round of rollouts and requires a privileged expert and a VLM annotator plus checker; there is no direct measure of trigger quality or recovery.
Simulation only, on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, and it does not beat DualVLN in SR on R2R.
